newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields rise following foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields rise following foreigners.

text.p: Swedish bond yields inched up in the early session on Monday in a slight foreign driven recoil from last week.
Dealers said continued worries over Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) also played a part.

"We are drifting along with foreign markets. It's a small recoil. We opened around the resistence level of 6.72 percent on the ten-year benchmark bond. If that had been broken yields would have fallen instead," one dealer said.
The ten-year bond yield rose four basis points to 6.77 percent.
The spread between Swedish and German long yields was flat at 101 and was expected to decrease.

"I think yields could increase further abroad, but Sweden will decrease its spread versus Germany. The rest of Europe is loosing ground on the EMU discussions, but countries such as Sweden will benefit relatively," one dealer said.
Six-month T-bill rates were unchanged at 4.12 percent and the crown was stable at 4.4630 against the mark compared to 4.4635 on Thursday.
